title: Joshua Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 16.

questions.question: From where did the lot of the children of Joseph fall?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 states that the lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho.

questions.question: Which mountain does the inheritance go up from Jericho?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 says the inheritance goes up from Jericho throughout mount Bethel.

questions.question: The border of the inheritance went out from Bethel to which place?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:2 states the border goes out from Bethel to Luz.

questions.question: Which border does the inheritance pass along to after Luz?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:2 shows the inheritance passes along unto the borders of Archi to Ataroth.

questions.question: Which coast does the border go down westward to?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:3 states the border goes down westward to the coast of Japhleti.

questions.question: Who took their inheritance according to Joshua 16?
options: Children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:4 clearly says that the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.

questions.question: True or False: The inheritance of the children of Joseph extends from Jordan by Jericho to the sea.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1-3 describe the borders extending from Jordan by Jericho to the sea.

questions.question: True or False: The lot of the children of Joseph included the wilderness going up from Jericho.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 states the lot included the wilderness going up from Jericho throughout mount Bethel.

questions.question: The border of the children of Ephraim on the east side included which of the following places?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:5 specifies that the eastern border of the children of Ephraim was Atarothaddar.

questions.question: Which place is mentioned as being on the north side of the Ephraim border?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:6 states the border went out toward the sea to Michmethah on the north side.

questions.question: True or False: The border went from Janohah to Ataroth and then to Naarath.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:7 says the border went down from Janohah to Ataroth, and to Naarath.

questions.question: Where did the border go out from Tappuah westward to?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:8 describes the border going out from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Ephraim drove out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 states they did not drive out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer.

questions.question: The separate cities for the children of Ephraim were found among the inheritance of which tribe?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 says the separate cities for Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh.

questions.question: In Joshua 16, which of the following locations is mentioned first in the border description?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 begins the border description with 'the lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho', making it the first mentioned location.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Joshua 16:5, what marks the east side border of the inheritance of the children of Ephraim?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:5 states that the border of their inheritance on the east side was Atarothaddar, unto Bethhoron the upper. This shows Atarothaddar as the starting point on the east side.

questions.question: How does the passage in Joshua 16:6 teach us about the importance of clearly defining boundaries and responsibilities in Christian living?
options: By showing the exact borders from Michmethah to Janohah, emphasizing order and clarity
By instructing to ignore borders and focus on unity only
By listing cities without any borders, emphasizing flexibility
By describing a chaotic border with no clear lines
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the exact borders from Michmethah to Janohah, emphasizing order and clarity
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:6 details the border from Michmethah on the north side, eastward to Taanathshiloh, and to Janohah, demonstrating the biblical principle of setting clear limits and responsibilities, which can be applied to integrity and order in Christian life (Joshua 16:5-7).

questions.question: What does Joshua 16:7 reveal about the border's connection to significant locations and what does this teach about faithfulness in following God's guidance?
options: It extends down to Jericho and Jordan, indicating obedience to God's allotment
It avoids Jericho and Jordan, showing independence
It disrespects Jericho by ignoring it
It crosses into enemy lands unlawfully
questions.correctAnswer: It extends down to Jericho and Jordan, indicating obedience to God's allotment
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:7 mentions the border going down from Janohah to Ataroth, Naarath, and then to Jericho and Jordan, reflecting faithfulness and trust in God's established boundaries for inheritance (Joshua 16:5-8).

questions.question: According to Joshua 16:8, where does the border go after leaving Tappuah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:8 states the border went out from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah, marking the western boundary of Ephraim’s inheritance.

questions.question: What lesson about coexistence and submission can be drawn from Joshua 16:10, where the Canaanites were not driven out?
options: Sometimes believers must live with imperfect circumstances and submit in humility
Believers should always drive out all opposition
Coexistence is never allowed in biblical teaching
The passage encourages total conquest without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Sometimes believers must live with imperfect circumstances and submit in humility
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 shows the Canaanites were not driven out but served under tribute, teaching the value of humility, submission to God’s timing, and living peaceably despite challenges.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 16:9 states that the cities of Ephraim were completely separate from the inheritance of Manasseh.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 explains that the separate cities for Ephraim were among the inheritance of Manasseh, not completely separate from it.

questions.question: What does the border described in Joshua 16:5-8 teach us about the importance of family and community inheritance in God’s plan?
options: That inheritance was organized carefully by families to preserve community and faithfulness
That inheritance was given randomly without consideration of families
That inheritance was only spiritual, not physical
That inheritance boundaries were ignored in favor of personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: That inheritance was organized carefully by families to preserve community and faithfulness
questions.explanation: The verses Joshua 16:5-8 detail inheritance borders according to families, showing God’s design for order, responsibility, and community preservation.

questions.question: A believer struggles with maintaining boundaries in their life. Based on Joshua 16:5-8, what biblical truth applies?
options: Setting clear and God-ordained boundaries brings order and blessing
Ignoring boundaries leads to spiritual growth
Boundaries are only physical, not spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: Setting clear and God-ordained boundaries brings order and blessing
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:5-8 shows God’s careful distribution of land with defined borders, teaching that boundaries are important for order and blessing in life.

questions.question: True or False: The border of Ephraim’s inheritance included passing by Taanathshiloh on the east, as described in Joshua 16:6.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:6 clearly states the border went about eastward unto Taanathshiloh and passed by it on the east, confirming this as part of the boundary.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue does the description of the border going out to the sea in Joshua 16:3 and 16:8 illustrate?
options: Faith in God’s provision extending beyond visible limits
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God’s provision extending beyond visible limits
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:3 and 16:8 mention borders going out to the sea, symbolizing trusting God to provide and protect even at the edges of known territory.

questions.question: How does Joshua 16:4 emphasize the importance of unity among the children of Joseph?
options: By stating that Manasseh and Ephraim together took their inheritance
By dividing them strictly with no cooperation
questions.correctAnswer: By stating that Manasseh and Ephraim together took their inheritance
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:4 highlights the unity of Joseph’s descendants—Manasseh and Ephraim—taking their inheritance together, illustrating the value of family unity and shared blessing.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 16:1, the lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho to the wilderness that goes up from Jericho throughout mount Bethel.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 explicitly states that the lot of Joseph's children fell from Jordan by Jericho unto the wilderness going up from Jericho throughout mount Bethel.

questions.question: What does Joshua 16:2 teach about the importance of recognizing landmarks and borders in spiritual and practical life?
options: It mentions the border going from Bethel to Luz and to Archi, showing the importance of clear guidance
It teaches to disregard physical boundaries
It focuses only on spiritual, not physical landmarks
questions.correctAnswer: It mentions the border going from Bethel to Luz and to Archi, showing the importance of clear guidance
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:2 describes the border passing through specific places, demonstrating the biblical principle of recognizing clear markers for direction and order.

questions.question: Which virtue is illustrated by the children of Ephraim not driving out the Canaanites in Joshua 16:10, yet having them serve under tribute?
options: Humility and patience in dealing with imperfect circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and patience in dealing with imperfect circumstances
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 reveals that the Ephraimites allowed Canaanites to dwell among them under tribute, teaching humility and patience rather than immediate conquest.

questions.question: What does Joshua 16:9 teach about the relationship between the cities of Ephraim and Manasseh?
options: The cities of Ephraim were located among the inheritance of Manasseh
Ephraim and Manasseh’s cities were completely separate
Manasseh’s cities were within Ephraim’s territory
The cities were not assigned to any tribe
questions.correctAnswer: The cities of Ephraim were located among the inheritance of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 states that the separate cities for Ephraim were among the inheritance of Manasseh, indicating an interwoven inheritance and cooperation.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 16.

questions.question: According to Joshua 16:9, where were the separate cities for the children of Ephraim located?
options: Among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: Among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 states that the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, including all the cities with their villages.

questions.question: What was the status of the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer according to Joshua 16:10?
options: They dwelt among the Ephraimites and served under tribute
They were enslaved by the children of Manasseh
questions.correctAnswer: They dwelt among the Ephraimites and served under tribute
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 explains that the Canaanites were not driven out from Gezer but dwelt among the Ephraimites and served under tribute to them.

questions.question: Which tribe's inheritance included cities that were located among the inheritance of another tribe, according to Joshua 16:9?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 specifically states that the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of incomplete driving out of the Canaanites as seen in Joshua 16:10?
questions.explanation: Judges 1:29 recounts that the children of Judah also did not drive out the Canaanites completely, echoing the theme in Joshua 16:10 where the Ephraimites did not drive out the Canaanites in Gezer.

questions.question: In the context of Joshua 16, the Hebrew word translated as 'serve under tribute' in verse 10 most closely means:
options: To be subjugated and pay taxes
questions.correctAnswer: To be subjugated and pay taxes
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'serve under tribute' implies subjugation involving payment or service, indicating the Canaanites paid tribute to the Ephraimites as per Joshua 16:10.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily observed in the juxtaposition of the Ephraimites’ inheritance being within Manasseh’s territory and their coexistence with Canaanites in Joshua 16?
questions.explanation: The presence of Ephraimite cities within Manasseh’s allotment and the unresolved presence of Canaanites creates a framing device or inclusio highlighting incomplete conquest and intermingling, as seen in Joshua 16:9-10.

questions.question: Which tribe specifically did Joshua 16:9-10 describe as having not driven out all the Canaanites from their allotted cities?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 states that the children of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer, who remained and served under tribute.

questions.question: The failure to drive out the Canaanites completely as recorded in Joshua 16:10 is often understood as a foreshadowing of what recurring problem in Israel's history?
options: The continual idolatry influenced by Canaanite practices
The division of the kingdom into north and south
questions.correctAnswer: The continual idolatry influenced by Canaanite practices
questions.explanation: The incomplete conquest and coexistence with Canaanites often led Israel into idolatry and syncretism, which is a recurring issue in later biblical history, foreshadowed by Joshua 16:10.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects on the theme of God’s promises and inheritance, as seen with the children of Joseph receiving their land in Joshua 16:4?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:9-10 discusses the faith of the patriarchs looking for a city with foundations, connecting to the theme of inheritance and God’s promises as in Joshua 16:4 where Joseph’s children take their inheritance.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 16:9, the cities of Ephraim were completely separated from the territory of Manasseh.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 explicitly states that the separate cities for Ephraim were among the inheritance of Manasseh, indicating they were not completely separated but intermingled.

questions.question: True or False: The 'river Kanah' mentioned in Joshua 16:8 marks part of the western border of Ephraim's inheritance.
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:8 describes the border going from Tappuah westward to the river Kanah, marking part of the western boundary of Ephraim’s inheritance.

questions.question: Which verse in Joshua 16 describes the border of Ephraim as extending 'to the sea'?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:8 says, 'The border went out from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah; and the goings out thereof were at the sea,' describing Ephraim’s border reaching the sea.

questions.question: In Joshua 16:5-7, which cities are mentioned that define part of Ephraim’s border?
options: Atarothaddar, Bethhoron the upper, Michmethah, Taanathshiloh, Janohah
questions.correctAnswer: Atarothaddar, Bethhoron the upper, Michmethah, Taanathshiloh, Janohah
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:5-7 describes the border of Ephraim including Atarothaddar, Bethhoron the upper, Michmethah, Taanathshiloh, and Janohah among others.

questions.question: How does the incomplete conquest of Canaan in Joshua 16:10 relate to the broader theme of obedience in the book of Joshua?
options: It illustrates the consequences of partial obedience to God's commands
It shows God's forgiveness despite disobedience
It celebrates the successful conquest of all enemies
It focuses on the establishment of the priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the consequences of partial obedience to God's commands
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10's record of not driving out the Canaanites highlights a recurring theme in Joshua: partial obedience leads to ongoing problems, showing consequences of incomplete faithfulness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage contains a prophecy that the land would be divided among the tribes of Joseph, similar to the allotment described in Joshua 16:4?
questions.explanation: Genesis 48:5 records Jacob blessing Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh, promising them an inheritance among the tribes, which is fulfilled in Joshua 16:4.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Joshua 16:1, from what location did the lot of the children of Joseph fall?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 clearly states that the lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho, indicating the starting boundary of their inheritance.

questions.question: What cities mark the eastern border of the inheritance of the children of Ephraim as described in Joshua 16:5?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:5 specifies that the border on the east side for the children of Ephraim was Atarothaddar unto Bethhoron the upper, marking the eastern boundary of their inheritance.

questions.question: Which tribe’s inheritance included cities that were geographically within the territory of another tribe, according to Joshua 16:9?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:9 reveals that the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, showing the complexity of tribal boundaries and inheritance.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the fact that the children of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites dwelling in Gezer, as seen in Joshua 16:10?
options: The doctrine of sanctification and incomplete obedience
The doctrine of justification by faith
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sanctification and incomplete obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 shows that the Ephraimites failed to fully drive out the Canaanites, illustrating the ongoing process of sanctification and the consequences of incomplete obedience to God's commands (cf. Hebrews 12:1-2).

questions.question: How does Joshua 16:4 reflect God's faithfulness in fulfilling His promises to Israel?
options: Children of Joseph, Manasseh, and Ephraim took their inheritance as promised
Israel wandered in the wilderness for 40 years
questions.correctAnswer: Children of Joseph, Manasseh, and Ephraim took their inheritance as promised
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:4 shows that the children of Joseph, including Manasseh and Ephraim, took possession of their inheritance, fulfilling God's covenant promise to give the land to Israel (cf. Genesis 48:19).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the precise and detailed allotment of tribal borders in Joshua 16:6?
options: God’s justice and faithfulness in covenant keeping
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and faithfulness in covenant keeping
questions.explanation: The detailed description in Joshua 16:6 reflects God’s just and faithful nature in allocating land to His people according to His promises, demonstrating His covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Joshua 16:7 and 16:8 provide about the nature of God’s providence in Israel’s settlement?
options: God’s providence ensures both boundaries and natural resources for His people
God’s providence is limited to spiritual blessings only
God’s providence is contingent on human military strength
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence ensures both boundaries and natural resources for His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:7-8 describe boundary lines and access to rivers and the sea, showing God’s providence in providing a secure and resourceful inheritance for Israel’s tribes.

questions.question: How does the presence of Canaanites serving under tribute in Joshua 16:10 typify the ongoing spiritual struggle within the people of God?
options: It symbolizes the coexistence of sin and grace within God’s people
It shows that God's people are free from temptation
It means that the Canaanites were fully converted
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the coexistence of sin and grace within God’s people
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 illustrates that despite God’s blessings, the Ephraimites lived alongside Canaanites who served them under tribute, symbolizing the mixed reality of sanctification where sin remains but grace prevails.

questions.question: What does the allocation of the inheritance to Joseph’s sons in Joshua 16:4 reveal about God's covenantal faithfulness to the descendants of Abraham?
options: God faithfully fulfills His promises to Abraham's descendants
God’s promises are conditional and often unfulfilled
God’s covenant was transferred to another nation
God’s promises only pertain to spiritual blessings
questions.correctAnswer: God faithfully fulfills His promises to Abraham's descendants
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:4 confirms that Joseph’s descendants, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance, affirming God's unwavering covenantal faithfulness to Abraham's lineage (cf. Genesis 17:7).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the presence of Canaanites in Ephraim's land (Joshua 16:10) disproves the Bible's teaching of God's complete victory over sin and evil. What does Joshua 16:10 actually teach?
options: God allows remaining sin and evil as a test and to fulfill His sanctification process
God failed to defeat evil in Israel
The Bible contradicts itself about conquest
The Canaanites were actually Israelites in disguise
questions.correctAnswer: God allows remaining sin and evil as a test and to fulfill His sanctification process
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:10 shows that the Ephraimites did not fully drive out the Canaanites, indicating God’s allowance of ongoing spiritual struggle and sanctification rather than a complete eradication of evil at once (cf. Romans 7:15-25).

questions.question: What theological truth arises from comparing Joshua 16:1 and 16:3 regarding God’s provision for His people?
options: God’s provision is both territorial and access to vital natural resources
God’s provision is arbitrary and without order
God’s provision excludes access to water
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision is both territorial and access to vital natural resources
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:1 and 16:3 together highlight that God’s provision to Israel included specific territorial boundaries and access to water bodies, essential for life and flourishing.

questions.question: What attribute of God is primarily revealed through the inheritance allotment to Ephraim and Manasseh in Joshua 16:4?
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:4 shows that God faithfully fulfilled His promise to Joseph’s sons by allotting their inheritance, demonstrating His unwavering faithfulness.

questions.question: How do Joshua 16:6 and 16:7 together demonstrate God's sovereign control over Israel's geographical destiny?
options: They provide precise boundaries that show God’s sovereign hand in shaping Israel’s land
They indicate Israel conquered land by their own strength alone
They show God was uninvolved in land distribution
They reveal that Israel’s borders were fluid and undefined
questions.correctAnswer: They provide precise boundaries that show God’s sovereign hand in shaping Israel’s land
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:6-7 give detailed boundaries for Ephraim’s inheritance, illustrating God’s sovereign control and purposeful design in Israel’s territorial allotments (cf. Psalm 24:1).

questions.question: What narrative arc does Joshua 16 contribute to within the broader biblical story of redemption?
options: The fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham through the possession of the Promised Land
The fall of man and entrance of sin
The establishment of the Davidic monarchy
The exile of Israel to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: The fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham through the possession of the Promised Land
questions.explanation: Joshua 16 focuses on the allotment of land to Joseph’s descendants, continuing the narrative of God fulfilling His covenant with Abraham by giving His people the Promised Land (Genesis 15:18-21).

questions.question: What combined teaching do Joshua 16:5-6 and Joshua 16:8 convey regarding God’s justice and order in His kingdom?
options: God establishes clear, just boundaries and order among His people
God's kingdom is chaotic and without structure
God’s justice is limited to spiritual matters only
God arbitrarily distributes land without regard to families
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes clear, just boundaries and order among His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 16:5-6 and 16:8 describe specific territorial borders for Ephraim, showing God's ordained justice and order in distributing inheritance among His people.
